subject: Banking
title: Car Loans at the Dealership
description: Learn Car Loans at the Dealership in one minute.

hook.text: 80% of car buyers finance through the dealership, not their bank.

buildup.text: Dealerships partner with lenders who provide instant approval.

discovery.text: Dealers earn a kickback by marking up the interest rate. A bank may approve 5% but the dealer quotes 7%, pocketing 2%.

twist.text: Online platforms like MakeMyDeal show transparent rates. Informed buyers negotiate better.

climax.text: Embedded car financing is convenient but opaque. The price of ease is often a quietly inflated interest rate.

punchline.text: 80% finance at the dealer. Convenience hides a 2% markup.

quiz.question: How do car dealerships profit from embedded financing?
options: Marking up lender interest rates and keeping the difference

details.summary: Embedded auto financing lets customers secure car loans directly at the dealership through digital platforms connected to multiple lenders, transforming the car-buying experience by integrating financing seamlessly into the purchase flow.
details.whyItMatters: Dealership financing demonstrates how embedded finance works in practice. When lending is integrated into the purchase experience, consumers make faster decisions and lenders reach customers at their highest moment of intent to borrow.
takeaways: Dealerships connect to multiple lenders via automated platforms
Digital financing approval can happen in minutes at the point of sale
Embedded lending captures borrowers when purchase intent is highest

faq.question: Is dealership financing more expensive than getting your own loan?
faq.answer: Often, yes. Dealers may mark up the interest rate from what the lender offers, keeping the difference as profit. Shopping for pre-approval from a bank or credit union before visiting the dealer often secures a lower rate.

faq.question: How is embedded auto finance changing?
faq.answer: Digital platforms now let buyers compare multiple loan offers in real time at the dealership. Fully online car purchases with integrated financing are eliminating the traditional back-office negotiation that dealers historically controlled.
